trickyParts: A repaint must never take a view block's iframe out of the document: an iframe that leaves it, even for an instant, loads again, and the block reads a second load as 'the page moved away', which is permanent. MarkdownBody.tsx therefore splices rather than replaces, pairing children that hold a frame slot by (page, ordinal) at each level and falling back to replaceChildren on any mismatch. The forward merge with main created a second painter, paintBlockInSlices, which ends by attaching a freshly built tree; a body holding a frame slot is now spliced at the attach, in one task. Proven with its own negative control: with those four lines removed, a repaint of a body over markdownWorkerThreshold gives two frame starts.

The 16 MiB cap was applied only on the render's scheduling effect, while a page's own dispatch-view:ready called schedule() straight from the message handler with no cap check, so a block over the cap printed its line and then read and posted the data anyway. The acceptance row passed before only on timing and failed the moment the lazy import changed it. schedule() now holds the cap too. 46 bytes.

A data file whose bytes are not UTF-8 text used to drop the whole dispatch-view:data message, because the read was written .then(onFulfilled, onRejected) and a sibling rejection handler never catches its own fulfilment handler's throw. Each file's read now distinguishes three outcomes — a status that is not ok (carrying its status), a fetch that rejected, and bytes that are not UTF-8 text — and the reader gets a line for each, which disappears when a later read of that file answers its text.

The editor's view slots were held in a module-global store, so with a version view open over the live editor (ProofDocument leaves its editor mounted-but-hidden) every slot received two ViewBlock subtrees and the element-keyed frame budget kept only the later callback. Fixed with the per-editor registry the ask block already uses, and locked by the row 'a view block is drawn once in a version view open over the live editor', which fails before the fix with toHaveCount Expected 1 Received 2.

The two summary terms were two descents of the same key and are now one lateral join. The grants list computed a per-row MIME probe nothing read.

WebKit cannot launch in a Legion issue pod: its system libraries are absent (libgstreamer, libgtk-4, libgraphene and twenty more), playwright install-deps cannot find the packages, and apt-get cannot take dpkg's lock as an unprivileged user. The webkit and webkit-iphone projects list 32 view rows each and run only in CI.
deviations: D1, carried from the plan: both summary reads gained the latest version's size, because the block must apply the 16 MiB cap before it fetches bytes and the reads carried no size.

D2, carried from the plan: a view block's attributes are indexed, so the block makes a mentions edge to its page and data files. Accepted rather than suppressed; one acceptance line (A1.6) asserts it.

D3, carried from the plan: this pull request repairs packages/envoy/migrationid/migrationid.go, which recorded Dispatch's numbered series as closed at 0157 while main carries 0158 to 0161. main was red for it and this tree adds a migration to the same set.

The data message's error vocabulary is wider than the spec's table, which names only not-granted. One entry per data file is the table's own rule, so a file that is not found, is not UTF-8 text, or whose read failed each carries a code too (unreadable, not-text, read-failed with its status). The architect ruled this accepted and required the skill to document every code; the spec is unchanged.

The renderer and the grants panel's body are loaded only where they draw, at the project controller's instruction. It costs A5 216 bytes, because A5 measures the one page that does hold a view block, and takes 7,815 bytes off the entry chunk that every other page fetches.

A5's byte budget is not met: 13,384 bytes of growth against a limit of 10,000. The row is red at its pinned base with nothing weakened. The limit is an approved acceptance value, so the architect has put it to the human in a decision block (dispatch://INFRA-682/ask/fa4e3094-4deb-4bc9-afe5-84dfcfc0e203), which proposes 14,000.
openQuestions: R6's 10,000-byte limit, with the human. Until it is answered the A5 byte row is red at head and the pull request cannot merge on a green run.
Whether a wider error vocabulary in the data message should also be reflected in the spec's own message table, or left as the architect's ruling records it.
discoveredComplexity: A view node inside a pending suggestion starts no second frame: its replacement is a ProseMirror decoration holding plain text, so the directive shows as its source and never reaches the node view. A suggestion over a document that already holds a view block keeps that block's frame running. This answers the plan's D8 check; no action was needed.

A comment body long enough to be clipped shows the clipped preview, which draws no frame, so a row about a comment's block opens the thread first; on the phone layout that thread is a dialog that mounts a second card under the same data-turn, and only the one holding the block's section draws the body.

PATCH /api/v1/comments/{id} is human-only and refuses anyone but the author, so 'another session's edit of the comment' is a second API session of the same person, beside the tab that is watching. If the spec means an agent must be able to edit a comment that holds a block, that is a server change.
